elements.element: Governing law is the laws of the State of New York
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction" (28.1 and 28.2)

elements.element: Governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales
elements.evidence: "the laws of the State of New York" — New York is the preferred, not fallback, law

elements.element: Corresponding forum: Delaware/California courts or the courts of London
elements.evidence: "courts located in New York County, New York"

offending_extra_words: and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.
reasons: Preferred level is fully satisfied: 28.1 now selects New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, a permitted corresponding pair.
The fallback bargain (Delaware/California or England and Wales with London courts) is not the level chosen, and correctly so given the locked target is preferred.

Minimality fails: 28.2 already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County, so re-stating the forum in 28.1 duplicates existing protection. Replacing only 'Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction' with 'the laws of the State of New York' (deleting the conflicting Singapore forum without restating the New York venue) would have sufficed; the official minimality gate flagged the 13-to-27-word expansion.

Intent is preserved: the Singapore/New York venue conflict is resolved, the submission to personal jurisdiction, venue waiver, and injunctive-relief carve-out in 28.2 remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
